title: install_7z.py passes the NSIS /D= folder as a quoted argument, which fails for a Windows user folder with a space
goal: install_7z.py runs the 7-Zip installer with /D=PATH unquoted and last on the command line, so a per-user folder that holds a space installs where it should

run:
t = open('_tools/install_7z.py', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert '"/D=" + str(dest.parent)]' not in t, 'the /D= folder is passed as one list argument, which Windows quotes when it holds a space'

repro_reason: the defect is how the Windows command line is built; this macOS host cannot run the NSIS installer, so the argument construction is what is read
notes: Review G3 of SP-iir3d2tu (plausible, Windows only, not run): install_7z.py:156 runs subprocess.run([installer, '/S', '/D=' + dest.parent]); NSIS documents /D= as unquoted and last.
